$comment: Compatibility manifest for the controlled downgrade (see the controlled-downgrade conception, lot A).
The CLI READS this file and never infers compatibility from a version number, so a release that is
not described here can only ever be told to restore from a backup -- which is the safe direction.
'from' is matched against /usr/share/bunkerweb/VERSION verbatim. BUMP IT WITH src/VERSION: a stale
'from' makes every pair unmatched and pins the product to restore_only. tests/unit/backup/
test_downgrade_manifest.py fails when the two disagree, so the bump cannot be forgotten silently.
MEASURED, per engine, by an executed upgrade+downgrade with sentinel data: `mode`, `data_loss`,
every `fingerprint` field, and each `restore_only` reason except where it says otherwise. A real
1.6.14 schema was built, seeded, upgraded to the 1.7 head, seeded again with 1.7-only rows and then
DERIVED, not measured: the `artifacts` map. It comes from reading the tree (src/common/helpers/data.sh
is byte-identical between v1.6.14 and 1.7, so the /data layout cannot have moved) and from what each
job regenerates, not from a downgrade run. Treat those values as a documented expectation.

fingerprint.method: 1.6.14 create_all -> stamp -> sentinel rows -> alembic upgrade head -> 1.7-only sentinel rows -> alembic downgrade to 1.6.14
fingerprint.baseline_row_delta_explained: +1: bw_ui_user_preferences is renamed back into bw_ui_user_columns_preferences rather than dropped
fingerprint.target_model_select_failures_detail: bw_ui_user_columns_preferences raised JSONDecodeError. An artifact of the probe's own sentinel, which wrote a non-JSON string into bw_ui_user_preferences.value before the downgrade renamed the table; real 1.7 preference values are JSON documents. The renamed-back rows still reach 1.6.14 as the wrong KIND of preference -- see the note below.

notes: Every table and column the 1.6.14 model declares is present after the downgrade, with no extras.

Non-column user preferences (theme_mode, whats_new, onboarding, walkthrough) reappear in 1.6.14 as bogus per-table column layouts: the downgrade renames bw_ui_user_preferences to bw_ui_user_columns_preferences wholesale instead of filtering the column-layout keys. Expected to be cosmetic rather than a crash, because every writer in src/ui/app/routes/ stores a JSON document -- but that is read off the callers, NOT measured: the probe's own sentinel was not JSON and did raise JSONDecodeError through the 1.6.14 model.

fingerprint.method: 1.6.14 create_all -> stamp -> sentinel rows -> alembic upgrade head -> 1.7-only sentinel rows -> alembic downgrade to 1.6.14
fingerprint.baseline_row_delta_explained: +1: bw_ui_user_preferences is renamed back into bw_ui_user_columns_preferences rather than dropped
fingerprint.target_model_select_failures_detail: Same as the sqlite row: bw_ui_user_columns_preferences raised JSONDecodeError on the probe's own non-JSON sentinel value, not on data the product writes.

notes: Two enum TYPES the 1.7 upgrade creates are not dropped by the downgrade (instance_tls_mode_enum, resource_kinds_enum), and the values added to api_resource_enum and settings_types_enum cannot be removed at all -- PostgreSQL has no ALTER TYPE ... DROP VALUE. Measured harmless: 1.6.14 never references them, the one SELECT failure the probe recorded is its own non-JSON sentinel (see target_model_select_failures_detail) and not these types, and a later re-upgrade is idempotent (CREATE TYPE ... EXCEPTION WHEN duplicate_object, ADD VALUE IF NOT EXISTS).
Those leftover values are also what SAVES PostgreSQL where MariaDB/MySQL fail: bw_ui_users.method keeps 'api' as a legal label instead of having the enum narrowed under it.

releases.reason: The 1.7 head's downgrade() does not run to completion on MariaDB. Two independent blockers. (1) Data-dependent, MEASURED here (dgad-probe-mariadb.json): ALTER TABLE bw_ui_users MODIFY method ENUM('ui','scheduler','autoconf','manual','wizard') fails with error 1265 'Data truncated for column method' on any row holding 'api', a value 1.7 added and the API sets. (2) Structural and data-independent, NOT reached by this lane's probe -- it aborts on (1) first -- and taken from lane LR-v's verification (report-LR.md 6.2, downgrade-exec-LR.log, which ran with no sentinel data and therefore got past (1)): DROP INDEX ix_bw_resource_group_usages_plugin_id fails with error 1553, 'needed in a foreign key constraint', on an index drop_table makes redundant. Both are byte-identical in the previous 1.7 beta heads and are never executed by product code. Worse than a plain refusal: the failure is partial. The first statement of downgrade() commits the bw_metadata version bump under MariaDB's non-transactional DDL, so a failed attempt leaves bw_metadata.version at 1.6.15~rc1 while alembic_version still names the 1.7 head and the schema is a hybrid -- a state the preflight refuses and the scheduler entrypoint cannot recover from. Restore from backup is the only path.

fingerprint.method: same probe as sqlite/postgresql; the downgrade aborted mid-way

releases.reason: The 1.7 head's downgrade() does not run to completion on MySQL 8 either. Blocker (1) was MEASURED separately here on a real MySQL 8 (dgad-probe-mysql.json): ALTER TABLE bw_ui_users MODIFY method ENUM(...) fails with error 1265 on a row holding 'api'. Blocker (2), the error-1553 index drop, is INFERRED for MySQL rather than measured: the probe aborts on (1) first, and lane LR-v's run covered MariaDB only. The two heads are byte-identical on that op, so it is expected to fail identically -- but nothing has executed it on MySQL. Either blocker alone is enough for restore_only. The version bump in bw_metadata has already committed when it aborts, so the database is left claiming 1.6.15~rc1 on a hybrid schema. Restore from backup is the only path.

fingerprint.method: same probe as sqlite/postgresql; the downgrade aborted mid-way

data_loss_detail.$comment: Applies to every in_place_tested pair above. 'certain' = the rows are destroyed and cannot be recreated; 'conditional' = destroyed but regenerable, with a stated cost. The preflight counts the live rows and compares them against this map.

why.bw_bans: regenerable by the sync-bans job, which relearns from the instances' shared dicts and Redis; ban durations and tombstones are lost
why.bw_ui_user_preferences: renamed back into bw_ui_user_columns_preferences rather than dropped, so the rows survive; only their meaning is lost (every key becomes a per-table column layout)
why.bw_ui_user_webauthn_credentials: every registered passkey; a passkey-only user must fall back to password + TOTP
why.bw_certificates: every centrally stored certificate and private key
why.bw_metrics_requests: all request metrics and the threat map history
why.bw_resources: every attachable resource, and by foreign key the redirects, upstream pools, workflows and resource groups keyed on it

data_loss_detail.columns_why: Dropped by the downgrade on every engine. The bw_instances credential and enrolment columns matter most: every enrolled instance has to be re-registered against the global API_TOKEN after a rollback.

not_counted_by_the_preflight.bw_metrics_baseline: observability, not configuration, and always non-empty -- counting it would pin every installation to restore_only forever
not_counted_by_the_preflight.bw_ui_user_preferences: every UI user has rows here (theme, dismissed notices, onboarding progress, what's-new stamps, column layouts), so counting it would pin every installation to restore_only. Not destroyed outright: the downgrade renames the table back to bw_ui_user_columns_preferences, so the rows survive and only their meaning is lost
not_counted_by_the_preflight.bw_resource_attachments: covered transitively: every row keys on bw_resources, which IS counted, so this table is empty whenever that one is
not_counted_by_the_preflight.bw_resource_group_entries: covered transitively: an entry keys on a group, and the operator-built groups ARE counted (bw_resource_groups WHERE plugin_id IS NULL). A seeded group cannot be given operator entries either -- update_resource_group refuses when method is not editable -- so what is left here is re-seeded by the next upgrade
not_counted_by_the_preflight.bw_resource_group_usages: a usage row is the index of which plugin consumes which group; it is rebuilt from the settings that reference the group, and those settings are 1.6.x rows the downgrade keeps. Not empty when a seeded group is in use, which is why it is not counted
not_counted_by_the_preflight.bw_upstream_servers: covered transitively: every row keys on bw_upstreams, which IS counted
